rationale: *Oerskovia merdavium*, 98.5% ANI, 90% aligned. Actinomycetota. Ferments glycerol and does not grow on L-lactate under either regime. One of the few carrying both glpK and glpF. 19 biosynthetic pathways, needs only biotin, catalase-positive. Electron recovery 1.0714 — a redox leak that does not localise, so its yields are unsafe, but that is a model defect and POOL_V4.md reached the same verdict independently: "strain probably fine, model is not". Carries tetB(58).

*Microbacterium* sp.; closest reference *M. forte* at 92.2% ANI, below the species threshold. Fastest glycerol growth in the pool once curation gave it the O2 transport it was missing — 0.066 to 0.534. Grows on L-lactate at 81% of its glycerol rate under air, so it is a strain to watch when oxygen is raised rather than one to exclude.

*Microbacterium* sp., 87.3% ANI — unplaced, not identified to species. Redox leak 1.083. Grows faster on L-lactate than on glycerol under air (1.69x), which is the strongest consumption signal in the pool and part of why oxygen is held low.

*Rhodococcus erythropolis*, 98.3% ANI. The best crude-glycerol profile in the pool by a wide margin — 49 LCFA genes, 23 halotolerance genes, 8 formaldehyde detox, total 86 against 34 for the next best. Its three lactate oxidases were the reason to be wary of it; they are O2-dependent, but quinone-linked L-lactate oxidation must also be retested whenever nitrate or another respiratory acceptor is supplied. Carries adhE, pta and ackA, so it can run the acetate/ethanol redox route.

*Lactococcus lactis*, 98.2% ANI. The only described lactate producer in the pool and the best LDH complement in the library — three L-LDH at 99.7-100% identity to characterized IL1403 ldh1/ldh2/ldh3, zero D-LDH. Chosen over the other six Lactococcus genomes because it is the only one whose model behaves like the organism: P3_B12 has no ATP synthase, and the other five cannot ferment glucose anaerobically. Carries adhE + pta + ackA. Two costs: a lactate oxidase (lctO, 48.1% to S. iniae, RBH-confirmed) that POOL_V4 records as absent, and 8 required supplements. Worst crude-glycerol robustness in the pool (halotolerance 3).

*Bacillus velezensis*, 98.8% ANI. Carried from pool v4 and survives every new filter. Cannot grow on L-lactate. Electron recovery exactly 1.0000. The only fully prototrophic member — zero requirements. Catalase 3. Pool v4 chose it for the best aerobic profile available: PDH present but no pyruvate oxidase and no NADH oxidase, so the least pyruvate and NADH diverted from lactate. Carries clbA at 99.1%, worth confirming since that family also contains housekeeping RlmN.

*Bacillus altitudinis* group — no direct ANI reference match. Current KEGG gene-content clustering pairs it only with P3_F11, and both share the B. pumilus- group resistance signature (blaBPU-1, cat86). It grows 1.8x faster on glycerol than P3_F11 and, unlike P3_F11, has modeled aerobic lactate-use capacity. Running both is a deliberate close-comparator test of whether that speed is worth the loss.
*Bacillus altitudinis*, 98.2% ANI, 95% aligned. Pool v4 producer. Cannot grow on L-lactate, recovery 1.0000, needs only biotin. The slow, clean half of the P1_F7 comparison.

*Paenibacillus taichungensis*, 98.6% ANI, 94% aligned. Zero requirements, 19 pathways, no lactate oxidase, recovery 1.0000. No glycerol facilitator — its model only grows because CarveMe attributed GLYCt to glpP, a transcriptional antiterminator that transports nothing. It has glpK, so glycerol is trapped as G3P on arrival and passive diffusion supplies it; expect a higher Ks, not an inability. P3_A10 is the same strain (>=99.5% ANI) and interchangeable.

*Paenibacillus amylolyticus*, 95.4% ANI. Redox leak 1.0161, marginal against a 1.015 tolerance and probably repairable. No glycerol facilitator, same as P3_A9. Carries adhE and nitrate respiration (narGH).

*Paenibacillus odorifer*, 97.1% ANI. No glpK at all — runs the oxidative route instead (gldA + dhaK: glycerol -> DHA -> DHAP), which traps glycerol just as effectively. Its model shows no growth on glycerol because no transport reaction was drawn, which is a modelling artifact rather than a finding: a genome-scale model cannot represent passive diffusion.

*Paenibacillus* sp.; closest reference *P. lupini* at 94.3% ANI, below the species threshold. Same situation as P3_C5 — no transport reaction, hence mu 0.0000, and it was excluded from an earlier pool on exactly that. It has glpK and the full catabolic route. Kept deliberately as the test of whether the model's no-growth verdict means anything.

Bacillaceae sp.; closest reference *Niallia tiangongensis* at 89.6% ANI, too low for a genus or species assignment. Redox leak 1.0244, the same value as P1_A3 whose leak localised cleanly to SUCD2, so probably repairable. Best formaldehyde detox in the pool (10) and strong metal resistance (9). Carries adhE + pta + ackA and fumarate respiration.

*Pseudomonas* sp. — species unresolved, no ANI hit against 392 reference species, so it is not a close relative of anything sequenced. Needs a family-level pass before publication. Cannot grow on L-lactate, recovery 1.0000, and it is the only Pseudomonadota producer, carrying most of the pool's phylogenetic spread. Background biosafety tier — nothing found, and the genus-list flag it used to carry does not survive evidence-based screening. Requires biotin, pantothenate, thiamine.

*Priestia aryabhattai*, 99.5% ANI, 94% aligned. Pool v4's keystone producer. Zero requirements, catalase 3, two amino-acid exporters, recovery 1.0000, cannot grow on L-lactate, background biosafety tier, and fourth-best crude-glycerol robustness. Held because it carries a complete larC1/larC2/larB/larE nickel-pincer cofactor operon plus a Lar_N-domain protein annotated "hypothetical protein" — the one failure mode that produces off-spec lactate with no D-LDH anywhere in the genome. Not proof: Lar_N scores 39.5 bits against 252.7 for a real LarA, LarA_C is absent, and the locus is flanked by uronate metabolism. One chiral HPLC injection on a monoculture supernatant decides it.

*Priestia megaterium*, 96.3% ANI. Same lar architecture as P1_B3 and the same hold. Also a long-standing industrial B12 producer by the anaerobic cbi* route, which is the route that runs under an O2-limited regime — so if the purity clears, this is the pool's B12 source rather than P3_C11. Carries lsa(B).
